column3: Close to the Hebrew; NKJV capitalizes “the Angel of the LORD” and pronouns for Him (throughout verses 11–22); “the terebinth tree” renders a word that may mean “the oak.”
Close to the Hebrew; “O my lord” renders “adoni,” a polite address.
Close to the Hebrew; “O my Lord” renders “Adonai,” as the Hebrew vowels mark it.
Close to the Hebrew; “Lord GOD” renders “Adonai YHWH.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The-LORD-Is-Peace” renders “YHWH Shalom.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the wooden image” renders “the Asherah” (also in verses 26, 28, 30).
